text:
olivia: Heads-up — canary for release/1.13.0 failed in CI during the DB migration step (migrate_users). Blocking promotion. https://ci.redwood.example/teams/infra/pipelines/1.13.0-canary/jobs/3456 :warning:
ci-bot: Pipeline started: release/1.13.0-canary (job 3456)
deploy-bot: Canary deploy started to cluster: canary-us-west1 on nodepool=g4dn-canary
olivia: Logs show a psql error deep in the migration — looks like migration ordering/race:```
2026-03-20T10:02:12Z migrate[1234]: applying 20260320_add_users_new.sql
psql: ERROR:  relation "users_new" does not exist
STATEMENT:  ALTER TABLE users_new ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS name text;
```
sanjay: Did this fail locally for anyone? I ran migrations against a snapshot and they passed for me.
marta: Not deterministic in CI — I see it intermittently in the last 5 runs (passed, failed, passed, failed). Looks like environmental ordering or cached artifact.
lee: We had a similar issue where cached built migration bundles meant old SQL landed after new ones. Clearing the build cache fixed it in that case. Could be the alpine base image + build cache.
olivia: Two short-term options: 1) pin the canary to previous image (1.12.9) and rollback canary to unblock release, or 2) force a migration-only rerun with cache disabled and then promote if green. Both require change-window approval if we do DB changes during peak.
sanjay: Kicking off a rerun with cache cleared now (job 3456 -> rerun #3456.1).
ci-bot: Rerun started: job 3456.1 (cache=false)
ci-bot: Rerun 3456.1 failed again — same psql relation error.
marta: Since rerun didn't help and this is blocking, I recommend rolling back the canary and pinning the release to 1.12.9 for promotion. We'll open a hotfix PR to add an explicit migration lock and sequence checks, and add a CI test that runs migrations twice on a fresh DB.
deploy-bot: Automatic rollback initiated to release/1.12.9-canary (reason: migration flake detected during canary).
olivia: I'll open the PR for the migration-lock patch and add an integration job in the pipeline (migration-smoke, runs on a clean DB with cache disabled). We should schedule the re-deploy outside the current change window (start at 02:00 UTC) once the fix and migration test are in.
lee: Also recommend a short-term mitigation to invalidate the builder cache for migration artifacts and pin the migration SHA in the release job.
sanjay: Ack — I'm on the hotfix PR and will coordinate the off-peak re-run.
marta: Noted. Tagging @eng-leads for visibility. :eyes:
